messages:
alisha: Quick question — after the model prune rollout yesterday we started returning a 'tombstone' signal for requests routed to deleted model variants. UX wants to know how we should present this to customers in the console and API. Do we treat it as 410, 503, or a new `X-Redwood-Tombstone` header?

ben: Short answer: don't use 503. It's noisy and triggers retries that waste capacity.

maria: Agreed. 410 (Gone) makes sense semantically, but we also want route-level telemetry to be able to surface whether this was a planned prune vs an unexpected deletion.

danielle: We could use 410 + header. Example suggestion: `HTTP/1.1 410 Gone` with `X-Redwood-Error: tombstone` and `X-Redwood-Tombstone-Reason: prune-scheduled` or `prune-unexpected`. Console can map reasons to badges.

alisha: That seems reasonable. Important to decide if clients should get a retry hint. If prune-scheduled -> no retry, prune-unexpected -> backoff + retry?

ben: Exactly. Retry hints should be explicit. I prefer an `Retry-After` for planned rollbacks only when we have an estimated ETA. Otherwise return `retryable: false` in the body/headers.

maria: For telemetry: we need a `tombstone.reason` tag (enum: scheduled, capacity-shift, deleted, unknown) and `tombstone.effect` (fallbacked, failed, routed-away). That will make dashboard filters easier.

devops-bot: deployment 2026-03-20T23:31:02Z: model-prune v3 completed on us-west-2. 42 variants tombstoned.

danielle: For the SDK surface, we should avoid forcing semantic parsing of headers. Provide a typed field in error payload: `{\n  "code": "MODEL_TOMBSTONED",\n  "detail": "variant 'm-7b-v2' removed by scheduled prune",\n  "retryable": false,\n  "meta": { "reason": "scheduled" }\n}`

alisha: Nice. Console UX: badging on routes -> 'variant removed' with hover text explaining recommended action (pin to newer variant / update deployment). Also show counts split by reason in the route view and a small CTA to open a rollout to re-route.

ben: One more: routing policy. When tombstone occurs, should traffic immediately fallback to the next compatible model or fail fast? My vote: for production routes, fallback if a compatible variant exists; for pinned routes, fail fast and emit `tombstone.pinned=true`.

maria: That aligns with our SLA tiers. We'll add `tombstone.fallback_allowed` bool to telemetry and error meta.

alisha: Action items: (1) eng-runtime: implement 410 + header + typed error payload and telemetry tags; (2) SDKs: expose typed `MODEL_TOMBSTONED` error with `retryable` and `meta`; (3) console: surface tombstone badges + reason filters; (4) product: write rollout guidance text.

ben: I'll open runtime PR with the headers and telemetry schema.

maria: I'll add the telemetry fields to the schema and a dashboard mock.

danielle: I'll update SDK error classes and docs.

alisha: Thanks all — let's sync again after PRs land. :thumbsup:
